stories.title: At least 12 dead as wildfires sweep through northern Algeria
stories.summary: At least 12 people have been killed and dozens injured as wildfires burn through large swathes of northern Algeria. Civil protection authorities said dozens of blazes swept through several provinces along the country's northern coastline. At least 54 people had suffered burn injuries, with at least six of them being treated in intensive care, Interior Minister Said Sayoud said on Wednesday night. The deaths comes as northern Africa swelters under a severe heatwave, with Tunisia and Algeria particularly affected. Sayoud said five people were killed in Jijel province, four in Bejaia and three in Tizi Ouzou. He has travelled to Bejaia with the Algerian Health Minister Mohamed Seddik Ait Messaoudene to "assess" local firefighting and evacuation efforts, government officials said. Many homes in Bejaia and Jijel have been evacuated, according to the civil protection agency and local media. Footage shared by local broadcaster Jijel News showed residents taking refuge in a post office as thick clouds of smoke billowed around them. Firefighters were battling 69 blazes across the country, the civil protection agency said earlier on Wednesday evening. The Bejaia region saw devastating fires tear through forest and farmland three years ago when 30 people were killed. Last month, authorities recorded at least six deaths caused by fires, with crews battling more than 2,000 blazes across Algeria in July alone. While Algeria regularly experiences forest fires around the summer months, climate change has exacerbated the intensity and severity of recent wildfires in the country.

stories.title: At least one dead after car crashes into crowd in northern France
stories.summary: At least one person has been killed and 10 people injured after a car crashed into a group of people near a train station in northern France, police say. One person had been arrested and taken into custody after authorities launched a major emergency response in Caen, in the Normandy region, local officials told the BBC. The incident took place near a bar, with local media reporting that a fight had broken out there before the incident took place. Social media videos from the scene appear to show crowds gathering around police cars and ambulances, where a large area is cordoned off. A spokesperson for the local administration of Calvados confirmed to the BBC that four people were receiving treatment in the emergency ward of a nearby hospital. Six others were being treated for less serious injuries, the spokesperson said. Detectives from Caen's Specialised Crime Division are leading the investigation. Locals have been told to avoid the area around the Caen train station.

stories.title: Plug-in balcony solar panels to go on sale in UK for first time
stories.summary: DIY system will be stocked by big retailers, starting with Argos, enabling more homes to lower bills by generating own electricity Plug-in solar panels will go on sale in the UK for the first time from Thursday, allowing households unable to use rooftop panels to also generate their own cheap electricity. Households across the country will be able to join the millions across mainland Europe who generate their own renewable electricity using “balcony solar panels”, which will be stocked by some of the UK’s biggest retailers. stories.title: Singapore police raid iron ore trader Radiant World over fake document claims
stories.summary: Singaporean police raided the local office of iron ore trader Radiant World last week and questioned some of the firm’s employees, according to people familiar with the matter, part of an investigation into the company’s transactions after some counterparties raised concerns about allegedly falsified documents. stories.headline: Singapore police raid iron ore trader Radiant World over fake document claims

opening: Singaporean police raided the local office of iron ore trader Radiant World last week and questioned some of the firm’s employees, according to people familiar with the matter, part of an investigation into the company’s transactions after some counterparties raised concerns about allegedly falsified documents.
Several major commodity traders have cut ties with the company amid concerns that it provided invoices or other documents to its banks that were not valid.
